A later development was to study how birds ate (ex tripudiis). Any bird would do (according to Cicero, On divination II, 34) but in practice special chickens were kept for the purpose by licensed handlers (pullarii). They were much used on military expeditions when wild birds might not be around and a quick answer was needed.

To consult them, the cage was opened and a piece of cake thrown in front of it. It was a bad sign if they declined to come out and eat it, or flew away, or flapped their wings and cackled, while it was a favourable omen if they tried to gobble it up and bits fell from their beaks.
